nodes.proof_route: Prove the scalar two-point L^(4/3)→L² inequality. Normalize weighted L^(4/3) norm to one; away from constants use strict Jensen and compactness, near constants use the uniformly positive second-order gap (exponent 4/3). Compact p∈[a,b] gives one r>0. This is only an inequality in two real variables and has no code, event, dimension, transitivity, derivative, or asymptotic assumptions. More concretely, divide the Jensen gap ((E|f|^(4/3))^(3/2)−(Ef)^2) by Var(f) on the compact unit sphere away from constants. The ratio has positive limit 1/3 at either constant ±1, uniformly for p in the compact interval. Any positive lower bound on this ratio supplies r².

alternative_proof_routes.route: Let δ=min(a,1−b)>0 and R=δ^(−3/4). Normalize E_p|f|^(4/3)=1, treating the zero-norm case separately; then |x|,|y|≤R because both atom weights are≥δ. On [−R,R], g(t)=|t|^(4/3) has g″≥(4/9)R^(−2/3) away from zero and continuous derivative at zero. Thus g(t)−c t² is convex for c=(2/9)R^(−2/3)=(2/9)√δ, established via monotonicity of g′−2ct, including the crossing-zero case. Strong Jensen yields 1−|Ef|^(4/3)≥c Var(f). Jensen also gives |Ef|≤1, so 1−(Ef)^2≥1−|Ef|^(4/3)≥c Var(f). Choose r=√c (positive and <1); then ||T_r f||²_2=(Ef)^2+r²Var(f)≤1. Undo normalization by homogeneity. This avoids compactness of a quotient near constants.

qualitative_route: Choose fixed 0<a<b<1. Let f be any upward indicator on m coordinates with equal influences for every p in [a,b]. Constants are trivial.
Russo and the mean value theorem give t∈(a,b) with total influence T=(μ_b−μ_a)/(b−a)≤B=1/(b−a). Equal influences give I_i=T/m≤B/m.
Parseval: variance=Σ_{S nonempty} fhat(S)^2. Energy: Σ|S| fhat(S)^2=t(1−t)T. The proved weighted_cutoff bounds the degree>k tail by t(1−t)T/(k+1).

Tensorized two-point contraction applied to D_i f∈{0,1} gives ||T_r D_i f||_2²≤I_i^(3/2). The exact noisy gradient identity bounds low degrees 1≤|S|≤k by t(1−t) r^(-2k)Σ I_i^(3/2); using r^(-2k) rather than r^(-2(k−1)) avoids the k=0 special case.
The proved influence_moment_bound makes the low term ≤t(1−t)r^(-2k)B sqrt(B/m). Using t(1−t)≤1 gives Var_t(f)≤r^(-2k)B sqrt(B/m)+B/(k+1).

Monotonicity gives μ_a(1−μ_b)≤μ_t(1−μ_t). For each fixed k the first bound tends to zero as m→∞ uniformly over events and groups. Then let k→∞. This yields the required uniform product limit without logarithmic rates.
For capacity at p=0 use the direct zero-erasure identity. For p>0 choose p<q<1−ρ and apply the Boolean theorem on [p,q]. No alphabet or field occurs anywhere in these Boolean lemmas.
